The Birth of
Immanent Critique
• The Spanish Empire claimed
universal jurisdiction, carrying
the banner of a unifying Catholic
truth into an unknown
hemisphere.
• Instead of universal order,
the Conquest unleashed

internal rivalry.

Empire of failing to live up to them.
The legacy of the New World is
not just colonization. It is the
centuries-long legal and moral
contestation over the definition
humanity, sovereignty, and law.

Dawn: Thousands of indigenous residents kneel
peacefully in the plaza as Spanish cavalry enters.
The Spark: A soldier inexplicably unsheathes his
sword. The massacre begins.

his horse, watching as if he were made of marble

priest, tends to the disemboweled, realizing the sheer
scale of the horror.
Y yo lo vi (I saw all this). Las Casas pioneered a
new form of political critique based on direct,
personal witness rather than abstract theology.

The Radical Alliance: Bidding for Sovereignty
In the 1550s, desperate for funds, King Philip considered allowing
settlers to buy their encomiendas outright -effectively turning Crown
wards into permanent chattel slaves.
The Settlers
Encomenderos offer
vast sums of gold to
Madrid to permanently

labor.
The Counter-Offer
Quechua leaders hold
emergency juntas and

Las Casas and Father

The Outcome: The Quechua offer to top the settlers' bid by 100,000 ducats to buy their
own freedom and dismantle the system. The sheer friction generated by this
indigenous-Dominican resistance forces the Crown to abandon the privatization plan.

America for Humanity
The history of the New World is a history of ideological contestation.
For the powers of the Global North, the Americas were a canvas for empire,
extraction, and proprietary dominion (America for America).
But for the magpies, the dissidents, and the revolutionaries- from Montesinos
to the modern era -the hemisphere possessed a redeemer mission.
They forged an immanent critique that demanded the New World live up to its
promise: not as a zone of conquest, but as the birthplace of human equality.
